key_insight: A reinforcement-learning workflow can generate and rank novel MOFs for photocatalysis by combining a CGCNN-based predictor funnel with a multi-objective fitness function.
engineering_relevance: The approach offers a scalable design pipeline for screening industrially relevant porous materials while balancing performance, stability, cost, and sustainability constraints.
method: Generated 60,000 novel MOFs with reinforcement learning.
Used a predictor funnel to iteratively filter candidates down to 10,986.
Trained CGCNN models to build a multi-objective fitness function and identify top-performing MOFs.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 20 designed materials that were 125% better than the control, including one Cr-based MOF with a 230% higher photocatalyst score and one Zn-based MOF that outperformed the best control across relevant metrics.
watch_item: Results depend on model predictions and abstract-level validation, so experimental synthesis and real-world stability testing are still needed before deployment.
paper_title: Machine Learning for Designing Undesignable Metal-Organic Frameworks
